title: Add SSE-driven RAG playground microfrontend and lightweight authoring templates
author: Aisha Malhotra
release_notes: Add a small SSE-based interactive RAG playground microfrontend, authoring templates for quick local iteration, and sample telemetry probes. No runtime API changes.
description: Context: Users asked for a tiny, low-latency local playground that demonstrates streaming token-level updates for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) without requiring WebSocket infrastructure. This PR introduces a server-sent-events (SSE) microfrontend and a set of lightweight authoring templates to accelerate developer onboarding and telemetry-driven debugging. Motivation: SSE provides a simple, firewall-friendly streaming transport that is easy to wire into static quickstarts and in-browser devsandboxes. The goal is a low-friction example that highlights streaming responses, prefix caching hints, and stepwise retrieval traces so engineers can reproduce production patterns locally. What this PR adds: 1) sse-playground/ directory with a minimal React microfrontend (300 lines) and a stubbed SSE server used by the quickstart; 2) templates/authoring/ containing two authoring presets (minimal and instrumented) for local iteration and replay; 3) examples/telemetry-probes.json with sample telemetry probes and suggested console dashboards; 4) docs/quickstarts/sse-rag-playground.md integrated into the quickstarts index and docs nav. Checklist: - [x] Microfrontend UI with streaming tokens and incremental highlights for retrieved snippets - [x] Local SSE server stub for developers (no external infra) - [x] Authoring presets with seed prompts and retrieval assertions - [x] Lightweight telemetry probes and example dashboards - [x] Docs page with quickstart steps and devcontainer entrypoint - [x] CI smoke test that runs the static build and validates SSE endpoint sanity Commit summary: - 7d8a2f3: add sse-playground React app and SSE client wiring - 5b1e4ef: add local stub server and start script, devcontainer snippets - c3f0b12: add authoring templates and telemetry probes - d9a67b0: docs page, links, and navigation entry Changed areas (high level): - sse-playground/src/App.tsx (stream token rendering, incremental HTML escape) - sse-playground/src/sseClient.ts (SSE event parsing and backpressure hints) - sse-playground/server/index.js (local stub server, sample event payloads) - templates/authoring/minimal.json and instrumented.json - docs/quickstarts/sse-rag-playground.md - examples/telemetry-probes.json - package.json scripts (start:playground, test:playground) Testing performed: - Manual end-to-end: local devcontainer, started stub server, verified token stream rendering and retrieval snippet inlined; stepwise latency simulated by server delays. - Unit: added small parser tests for SSE chunking and partial-event assembly. - CI: static build step and a node sanity check on the SSE endpoint.
Review conversation: Diego Santos: Nice lightweight approach, can we avoid introducing another runtime dependency? Suggest using native fetch EventSource on the client and keep node only for the devserver.
Aisha Malhotra: Good call — switched client to native EventSource and removed the small SSE polyfill; node server remains for dev only. Updated tests.
Eleanor Park: The telemetry probes look useful, please add one example dashboard screenshot and call out privacy guidance for embedded PII.
Aisha Malhotra: Added dashboard sample and a short privacy note in the docs; ensured probes are opt-in by default.
Marta Ivanov: Approved after nit on docs wording; please squash commits.
Aisha Malhotra: Squashed and updated the changelog entry.
Notes and migration: No API surface changes. This is an opt-in example; customers running private deployments are unaffected. The devcontainer is configured to run the stub server on startup for a one-command experience. If teams want to wire the playground to a real Redwood instance, the docs include a short section on auth tokens and SSE headers.
Example usage snippet: 1) git checkout feature/sse-rag-playground-quickstart 2) npm ci && npm run start:playground 3) open http://localhost:3001 and type a question — tokens stream as SSE events and retrieved snippets are highlighted.
Additional context: This PR purposely keeps the example small and focused on streaming ergonomics and observable traces rather than full production-grade orchestrations. Follow-ups planned: add a non-demo guide for wiring to Redwood Dedicated with SSE-to-WebSocket bridging patterns, and a small eval harness measuring prefix vs full-stream latency for typical RAG prompt sets.
